# Job Chapter 41 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folios 431v–432r

---

**41:1** "Can-you-draw-out [timshokh] Leviathan [livyatan] with-a-fishhook [be-chakkah]? And-with-a-cord [u-ve-chevel] can-you-press-down [tashqi'a] its-tongue [leshono]? **41:2** Can-you-put [ha-tasim] a-reed [agmon] in-its-nose [be-appo]? Or-with-a-thorn [u-ve-choach] can-you-pierce [tiqqov] its-jaw [lechyo]?

**41:3** Will-it-multiply [ha-yarbeh] to-you supplications [tachanumim]? Or will-it-speak [yedabber] to-you soft-words [rakkot]? **41:4** Will-it-make [ha-yikhrot] a-covenant [berit] with-you? Will-you-take-it [tiqqachenu] as-a-servant [le-eved] forever [olam]? **41:5** Will-you-play [ha-tesacheq] with-it like-a-bird [ka-tsippor]? Or will-you-bind-it [ve-tiqshrennu] for-your-girls [le-na'arotekha]?

**41:6** Will-companions [chaverim] bargain [yikhru] over-it? Will-they-divide-it [yechaltsuhu] among the-merchants [bein kena'anim]? **41:7** Can-you-fill [ha-temalle] its-skin [oro] with-barbed-irons [be-sukkot]? Or-its-head [ve-rosho] with-fish-spears [be-tsiltsol dagim]?

**41:8** Lay [sim] your-hand [kappekha] upon-it; remember [zekhor] the-battle [milchamah] — do-not-do-it-again [al-tosaf]! **41:9** Behold, any-hope [tohalato] of-him is-disappointed [nikhzavah]; even at-its-sight [el-mar'av] shall-one-not be-hurled-down [ha-lo yutal]?

**41:10** No-one [lo] [is so] fierce [akhzar] that-he-dares-stir-it [ye'urehu]; and-who [is] he [that] before-me [lefanai] can-stand [yityatsav]? **41:11** Who has-confronted-me [hiqdimani] and-I-will-repay [va-ashallem]? Under all the-heavens [ha-shamayim] — to-me [li] it [belongs] [hu].

**41:12** I-will-not be-silent [lo acharish] concerning-its-limbs [baddav], and-the-matter of-its-might [devar gevurot] and-the-grace [chin] of-its-frame [erkho].

**41:13** Who has-uncovered [gillah] the-face of-its-garment [levusho]? In-its-double [bi-khfel] bridle [risno], who can-come [yavo]? **41:14** The-doors [daltei] of-its-face [panav], who has-opened [pitteach]? Around [sevivot] its-teeth [shinnav] [is] terror [eimah].

**41:15** A-pride [ga'avah] [are its] rows of-shields [afiqei maginnim], shut-up [sagur] [with a] seal [chotam] tight [tsar]. **41:16** One to-another [be-echad] they-are-close [yiggashu], and-wind [ve-ruach] cannot-come [lo-yavo] between-them. **41:17** Each to-its-fellow [ish be-achihu] they-are-joined [yuddabbaqu]; they-clasp-each-other [yitlakedu] and-cannot-be-separated [ve-lo yitparedu].

**41:18** Its-sneezings [atishotav] flash-light [tahel or]; and-its-eyes [ve-einav] [are] like-the-eyelids of-the-dawn [ke-af'appei-shachar]. **41:19** From-its-mouth [mi-pihu] torches [lappidim] go [yahaloku]; sparks of-fire [kidodei-esh] escape [yitmallatu]. **41:20** From-its-nostrils [mi-nechirav] goes-out [yetse] smoke [ashan], like-a-boiling [napuach] pot [dud] and-rushes [ve-agmon]. **41:21** Its-breath [nafsho] kindles [telahhet] coals [gechalim], and-a-flame [ve-lahav] from-its-mouth [mi-pihu] goes-out [yetse].

**41:22** In-its-neck [be-tsavvaro] lodges [yalin] strength [oz], and-before-it [lefanav] leaps [taduts] dismay [de'avah]. **41:23** The-folds [mappelei] of-its-flesh [besaro] cling-together [davequ]; they-are-firm [yutsaq] upon-it [alav], immovable [bal-yimmot]. **41:24** Its-heart [libbo] [is] cast [yatsuq] like-stone [kemo-even], and-cast [ve-yatsuq] like-the-lower millstone [pelach tachtit].

**41:25** When-it-raises-itself [mi-seto] the-mighty [elim] are-afraid [yaguru]; from-the-crashing [mi-shevarim] they-are-beside-themselves [yitchatta'u]. **41:26** The-one-overtaking-it [massigeihu] — the-sword [cherev] cannot-prevail [beli-taqum]; the-spear [chanit], the-dart [massa], and-the-javelin [ve-shiryah].

**41:27** It-regards [yachshov] iron [barzel] as-straw [le-teven], bronze [nechusah] as-rotten-wood [le-ets riqqavon]. **41:28** The-arrow [ben-qeshet] cannot-make-it-flee [lo yavriechennu]; sling-stones [avnei-qela] are-turned [nehpekhu] to-it to-stubble [le-qash]. **41:29** As-stubble [ke-qash] the-club [toteach] is-regarded [nechshavu]; and-it-laughs [yis'chaq] at-the-rattling of-the-javelin [ra'ash kidon].

**41:30** Its-undersides [tachtav] [are] sharp potsherds [chaddei-chares]; it-spreads [yirpad] a-threshing-sledge [charutz] upon the-mud [alei-tit]. **41:31** It-makes-boil [yartia'ch] the-deep [metsulah] like-a-pot [ka-sir]; it-makes [yasim] the-sea [yam] like-a-pot-of-ointment [ka-merqachah]. **41:32** Behind-it [acharav] it-makes-shine [ya'ir] a-path [nativ]; one-would-think [yachshov] the-deep [tehom] [to be] white-haired [le-seivah].

**41:33** There-is-nothing [ein] on-the-dust [al-afar] like-it [mashlo] — the-one-made [he-asu] without [le-veli] fear [chat]. **41:34** All the-high [kol-gavoah] it-sees [yir'eh]; it [is] king [melekh] over all the-sons of-pride [benei-shachats]."

---
## EMET's Textual Notes

**v.1 — "Leviathan":** Hebrew *livyatan* — from *lavah* ("to twist/coil"). A sea monster appearing also in Psalms 74:14, 104:26, and Isaiah 27:1. In Canaanite mythology, *Litanu* was a seven-headed sea serpent defeated by Baal. Here God presents Leviathan not as defeated chaos but as his own creature — fearsome, magnificent, and utterly beyond human control.

**v.10-11 — "Who then can stand before me?":** God's argument pivots from creature to Creator. If no one can face Leviathan, how much less can anyone stand before the God who made it? Verse 11 — "Who has confronted me and I will repay? Under all the heavens — to me it belongs" — is the theological climax of the Leviathan passage.

**v.18-21 — Fire-breathing imagery:** The description of Leviathan sneezing light, breathing fire, and emitting smoke goes far beyond any natural animal. This is mythological language. Whether the original audience understood this as literal or poetic, the effect is the same: this creature is terrifyingly other.

**v.34 — "king over all the sons of pride":** Hebrew *melekh al-kol-benei shachats*. Leviathan reigns over everything that is proud and fierce. God's implicit point: only God is above this king, and therefore only God can govern pride.

*— EMET*
